style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=top;whiteSpace=wrap;fontColor=#8c8f98;fontSize=11;fontFamily=IBM Plex Sans;spacing=0;" value="A job is accepted once, by a unique key on the accepted-jobs row, then published. The reconciler republishes only rows with no publish receipt, so a crash between insert and publish loses nothing. Each (tenant, class) has its own small queue and the controller pulls with credit, so the broker never orders across tenants. Admission counts live jobs from the rows, commits the claim of the row from accepted to admitted before it starts the workflow, and acks a message whose row is already past accepted. Two scans read the rows too: one re-admits a job resumed before it started, whose message is gone, and one starts a row left admitted with no workflow. div.div: A job is accepted once, by a unique key on the accepted-jobs row, then published. The reconciler republishes only rows with no publish receipt, so a crash between insert and publish loses nothing. Each (tenant, class) has its own small queue and the controller pulls with credit, so the broker never orders across tenants. Admission counts live jobs from the rows, commits the claim of the row from accepted to admitted before it starts the workflow, and acks a message whose row is already past accepted. Two scans read the rows too: one re-admits a job resumed before it started, whose message is gone, and one starts a row left admitted with no workflow. Only intake messages that cannot be processed reach the DLQ, each with a reason that says how to recover it.
